primaryText: BOY ENTER CLUB. MUSIC ON. DANCE.
translation: A boy entered a club. Music went on. He danced.
comment: Accepted by all three signers (3/3). One referent; the final verb is unmodified.

primaryText: BOY ENTER CLUB. MUSIC ON. SEE GIRL READ. DANCE.
translation: Intended: A boy entered a club. Music went on. He saw a girl reading. He danced.
comment: Printed with (1/3): accepted by one of three signers. The paper gives consultant judgments as such counts ((11a) is * and 0/3), so the count is the mark; the prose calls two-referent narratives without loci degraded. Two referents, no loci established, unmodified verb.

primaryText: BOY IXA ENTER CLUB. SEE GIRL IXB READ. MUSIC ON. (IXA) DANCEA.
translation: A boy entered a club. Music went on. He saw a girl reading. He danced.
comment: 3/3. Two referents established in loci; the verb is signed at the agent's locus.

primaryText: SUE HANG-OUT MARY. PUSH.
translation: Intended: Sue and Mary were hanging out. Then she pushed her.
comment: Rejected by all three signers (0/3). No loci and no context making the agent salient.

primaryText: SUE IXA HANG-OUT MARY IXB. (IXA) PUSHB (IXB).
translation: Sue and Mary were hanging out. Then she pushed her.
comment: 3/3. Loci marked and the verb moves between them.

primaryText: SUE HANG-OUT MARY. MARY SAY SOMETHING BAD. SUE ANGRY. PUSH.
translation: Sue was hanging out with Mary. Mary said something bad. Sue got angry. She pushed her.
comment: 3/3: context suffices. The surrounding context renders the agent salient; the same unmodified verb as in (11a).
